reason: Checked on the operator's ask ("Check Paysafe for FE"). Paysafe is already on the Formula E grid, so it is sponsor-side, not a prospect. On 14 Aug 2026 Paysafe (NYSE: PSFE) became title partner of Envision Racing, the team racing as Paysafe Envision Racing into the GEN4 era; activations began at the London E-Prix 15-16 Aug 2026, with a livery reveal set for October 2026 and expanded programming across Season 13 (Business Wire / fiaformulae.com / envision-racing.com, all 14 Aug 2026). The company would in other respects have read as a candidate - Q2 2026 revenue $447.4M (+4% reported and organic), adjusted EBITDA $102.8M (-2%, margin 23% vs 24.5%), net loss $58.9M or $(1.13) per diluted share, adjusted net income $23.1M / $0.43, FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at 5-8% revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth (all REPORTED via search summaries; sec.gov and paysafe.com are egress-blocked from this sandbox) - but the capacity picture argues against a second multi-year deal in any case: net leverage 5.3x at quarter end, guided to 5.1-5.2x by year end against a mid-term target of roughly 3.5x, a refinancing that added about $25-35M of annual cash interest, and a market capitalisation near $340M at $6.52 (18 Aug 2026), i.e. a sponsorship budget already committed to the deal it just signed. Leadership as at this check: Bruce Lowthers, Chief Executive Officer (since May 2022); Alisa Barber, Chief Marketing Officer (since 2022); Daniel Henson, Chairman; Nicole Carroll, Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer. (An older Paysafe release names Oscar Nieboer as CMO - superseded, do not use.) The desk action is a sponsor-side / renewal-and-activation conversation through the Envision relationship, not a cold origination sequence. Re-open as a prospect only if the Envision title lapses.
